forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Tunbridge Wells draft budget shows £259,000 gap for 2027/28 after waste contract cost "nearly doubled"
news_drafts.lead:
Tunbridge Wells Borough Council's draft revenue budget for 2027/28 shows a deficit of £259,000, against nil in the approved 2026/27 budget. The figures are in the draft budget and its Appendix A, before the Finance, Innovation and Transformation Cabinet Advisory Board on 9 November 2026.

The draft budget says the gap is "largely due to the expiry of the waste and street sweeping contract on 31 March 2027, the cost of which has nearly doubled". It describes the new contract as the largest service contract the council has ever awarded, and as a major implementation project requiring professional advice and resources from across the council.

The paper says the 2027/28 deficit, "if left unmanaged, would need to be funded from reserves". It gives the forecast gap for 2028/29 as £1.8m if left unmanaged. Appendix A shows no line setting out how the £259,000 is to be met. The draft budget says the administration will set out its prioritisation of services before the final budget is set, and that the public will be asked to allocate funding in comparison with the draft.

news_drafts.headline: Tunbridge Wells forecasts 2027/28 budget gap of £801,000, down from £4.5m forecast in February
news_drafts.lead:
Tunbridge Wells Borough Council is forecasting a deficit of £801,000 for 2027/28, a budget update before its Cabinet on 22 October shows. In February, the council reported a forecast deficit of £4.5m for the same year to Full Council, so the forecast gap has fallen by about £4.0m.

The update gives two reasons for the change: the council has awarded major contracts, and it has been notified of the Local Government Finance Settlement, the government's annual funding announcement for councils. The paper says the remaining gap will need to be closed through further efficiencies and service changes.

The council's strategy on council tax is to raise it each year up to the referendum threshold, the level above which a council must hold a local vote on an increase. The update says: "This council has historically had a policy of very low council tax levels and the strategy is for council tax to increase up to the threshold for triggering a referendum." It says low existing bills leave room to do this. It also says the government assumes, in its own assessment of the council's finances, that the council will raise council tax by the maximum permitted.

news_drafts.headline: Tunbridge Wells cuts forecast 2027/28 budget gap to £801,000 from £4.5m reported in February
news_drafts.lead:
Tunbridge Wells Borough Council's forecast budget deficit for 2027/28, the gap between what it expects to spend and what it expects to have, has fallen to £801,000. In February the council reported a deficit of £4.5m to Full Council. The new figure is in a budget update going to the council's Finance, Innovation and Transformation Cabinet Advisory Board on 5 October.

The paper gives two reasons for the reduction: the awarding of major contracts, and the council being notified of the Local Government Finance Settlement, the government's annual announcement of funding for councils. The update says a deficit of £801,000 "is currently forecast for 2027/28, a decrease on the £4.5m reported to Full Council in February".

The gap has not yet been closed. The council's directors are continuing work on it through service planning and proposals for efficiencies. Officers are due to report back in December with draft proposals.

findings.committee: Finance, Innovation and Transformation Cabinet Advisory Board
findings.headline: Council tax income in the draft rises by £429,000, from £10,780,230 to £11,209,230.
findings.detail: The council tax line is shown in brackets as income. The variance is recorded as (429,000), meaning income rises by that amount in the draft. Collection fund surplus or deficit is held at (£62,000) in both years.
findings.matters: A finance director would compare this council tax increase against the total increase in the net budget requirement of £1,421,160.

findings.committee: Finance, Innovation and Transformation Cabinet Advisory Board
findings.headline: Mid Kent Client Services moves from a cost of £2,538,710 in 2026/27 to a credit of (£2,496,670) in the 2027/28 draft, a variance of (£5,035,380).
findings.detail: The largest variance in the table is this line's movement. The table presents the 2026/27 figure as a positive cost and the 2027/28 draft as a bracketed credit. The table does not explain the reason for the change.
findings.matters: A finance officer at a council with a shared-service arrangement would want to know how a movement of this size is being reflected in the budget.

findings.committee: Finance, Innovation and Transformation Cabinet Advisory Board
findings.headline: Head of Housing, Health & Environment rises from £7,129,150 to £10,628,790 in the draft, a variance of £3,499,640, the largest service increase in the table.
findings.detail: The budget sub-total per service rises by £3,497,510 overall. This service's variance of £3,499,640 is larger than that total, so the other services net to a reduction. The table does not give the cause of the increase.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council would want to compare how a single service's cost increase is absorbing the wider budget.
findings.figures: £7,129,150 (2026/27 approved); £10,628,790 (2027/28 draft); variance £3,499,640; budget sub-total per service variance £3,497,510

findings.committee: Finance, Innovation and Transformation Cabinet Advisory Board
findings.headline: The 5046/9 transfer to reserves line moves from £2,100,000 in 2026/27 to nil in the 2027/28 draft, a variance of (£2,100,000).
findings.detail: The table labels the line 'Transfer (from) to reserves'. The 2026/27 approved figure is £2,100,000 and the 2027/28 draft is zero. The table does not state the reason for the change.
findings.matters: A reserve movement of this size that drops out of the following year's budget changes the funding position a finance director must plan around.
findings.figures: £2,100,000 in 2026/27 approved; nil in 2027/28 draft; variance (£2,100,000)

findings.committee: Finance, Innovation and Transformation Cabinet Advisory Board
findings.headline: The draft 2027/28 revenue budget shows a deficit of £259,000, against nil in the 2026/27 approved budget.
findings.detail: The draft table's final line shows the revenue budget or deficit at 0 for 2026/27 and 259,000 for 2027/28. No line in the table shows how that £259,000 is to be met. The table itself does not explain the position.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council, or a lender, would want to know whether a draft budget with no balancing line is a deficit the council has not yet closed.
findings.figures: £259,000 deficit in 2027/28 draft; nil in 2026/27 approved
